questions.prompt: Why do economists today focus on price inflation rather than monetary inflation when discussing inflation?
options: Because price inflation is what people actually measure and discuss today.
Because monetary inflation no longer exists.
Because price inflation and monetary inflation are identical.
Because the money supply never changes.

questions.prompt: How does a supply shock in oil affect the price of unrelated goods such as bananas?
options: It only raises oil prices, not other goods.
It raises transportation costs, which increase prices of many goods including bananas.
It decreases banana prices because consumers switch away from oil.
It has no effect because bananas are not made of oil.

questions.prompt: In the simplified CPI example, if apple prices rise by 50% and banana prices rise by 80%, how is the overall CPI change calculated?
options: By averaging the two percentage changes equally (65%).
By weighting each percentage change by its expenditure share (62%).
By adding the two percentages together (130%).
By taking the higher of the two percentages (80%).

questions.prompt: A modest inflation rate of around 2% per year is generally considered beneficial because it allows prices to adjust gradually without causing economic instability.
The CPI-U index is calculated by giving equal weight to all goods in the consumer basket, regardless of how much of their income consumers spend on each good.
Why does an increase in the money supply that outpaces real productivity tend to cause price inflation?
Why is the CPI‑U considered the headline consumer price index reported in the news?
How does using the expenditure shares of apples (60%) and bananas (40%) to compute a weighted average of their price changes give the overall CPI change?
